First, we find the Laplace transforms of both sides of each equation in our system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}L{{x}_{1}^{′}(t)}=L{{x}_{1}(t)-2{x}_{2}(t)} \\ L{{x}_{2}^{′}(t)}=L{-{x}_{1}(t)+2{x}_{2}(t)}\end{aligned}\,\,
$$

Using the derivative property of the Laplace transform, we obtain the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}sL{{x}_{1}(t)}-{x}_{1}(0)=L{{x}_{1}(t)}-2L{{x}_{2}(t)} \\ sL{{x}_{2}(t)}-{x}_{2}(0)=-L{{x}_{1}(t)}+2L{{x}_{2}(t)}\end{aligned}
$$

which can be simplified to the following:

$$
{\begin{aligned}s{X}_{1}(s)-9={X}_{1}(s)-2{X}_{2}(s) \\ s{X}_{2}(s)-6=-{X}_{1}(s)+2{X}_{2}(s)\end{aligned}
$$

where ${X}_{1}(s)=L{{x}_{1}(t)}$ and ${X}_{2}(s)=L{{x}_{2}(t)}.$

Rewriting the system in standard form, we get the following:

$$
{\begin{aligned}(s-1){X}_{1}(s)+2{X}_{2}(s)=9 \\ {X}_{1}(s)+(s-2){X}_{2}(s)=6\end{aligned}
$$

Now, from the second equation, we have 

$$
{X}_{1}(s)=6-(s-2){X}_{2}(s).
$$

Substituting this into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(s-1)[6-(s-2){X}_{2}(s)]+2{X}_{2}(s) & =9 \\ 6(s-1)-[(s-1)(s-2)-2]{X}_{2}(s) & =9 \\ -({s}^{2}-3s){X}_{2}(s) & =9-6(s-1) \\ -s(s-3){X}_{2}(s) & =-6s+15 \\ {X}_{2}(s) & =\frac{3(2s-5)}{s(s-3)}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find ${X}_{1}(s):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{X}_{1}(s) & =6-(s-2){X}_{2}(s) \\  & =6-(s-2)\cdot \frac{3(2s-5)}{s(s-3)} \\  & =\frac{6s(s-3)-3(s-2)(2s-5)}{s(s-3)} \\  & =\frac{3(3s-10)}{s(s-3)}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
{X}_{1}(s)=\frac{3(3s-10)}{s(s-3)},\,{X}_{2}(s)=\frac{3(2s-5)}{s(s-3)}.
$$
